newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says UPS, Teamsters making progress.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says UPS, Teamsters making progress.

text.p: President Clinton said Sunday United Parcel Service and the Teamsters union were making progress in their talks and he urged them to redouble their efforts to settle the strike at the parcel company.
"It's clear that they're making progress," Clinton told reporters before boarding his helicopter to leave for vacation on Martha's Vineyard.
Clinton said he had just been briefed by Labor Secretary Alexis Herman and White House aide Bruce Lindsey on the talks between UPS and the Teamsters.

"I just want to urge them to redouble their efforts," Clinton said. "This strike is beginning to hurt not only the company but its employees and the people who depend on it and I think they ought to redouble their efforts to settle the strike and they ought to do it today."
Herman was directly involved in bringing the company and the union back to the negotiating table last week. Lindsey has been following the strike at the White House.

"I'm pleased by the progress that's been made and I hope they'll just stay there and settle it today," Clinton added. He, his wife Hillary and their daughter Chelsea then boarded the helicopter and left the White House.
